questions.stem: What is „ein Quereinsteiger“?
options: Someone who enters a career without the usual training for it
Someone who climbs quickly to the top of their company
Someone who changes schools in the middle of the year
Someone who commutes across the border to work each day
questions.explanation: „Quer“ means across, so a „Quereinsteiger“ comes into a profession from the side, for example an engineer who becomes a teacher. A cross-border commuter is „ein Grenzgänger“.

questions.stem: What is „das Abitur“?
options: A three-year apprenticeship in a trade or craft, completed with a firm
The certificate given at the end of primary school
An evening course for adults returning to study
The school-leaving qualification that opens the way to university
questions.explanation: „Das Abitur“ is usually taken at the end of the Gymnasium and qualifies a student for university. An apprenticeship is „eine Ausbildung“ or „eine Lehre“, a separate pathway that does not need the Abitur.

questions.stem: What does „die Selbstverwirklichung“ mean?
options: Self-employment, running one's own business
Self-discipline, controlling one's own habits
Self-defence, protecting oneself from attack
Self-fulfilment, realising one's own potential
questions.explanation: „Sich verwirklichen“ is to realise oneself, so the noun is self-fulfilment. It is a frequent value in discussions of careers and work-life balance.

questions.stem: What is „ein Arbeitszeugnis“?
options: A written reference from an employer describing an employee's work
A certificate showing the school subjects a student has completed
A contract setting out an employee's hours, pay and holidays
A record of the hours an employee has worked each week
questions.explanation: „Das Arbeitszeugnis“ is issued when someone leaves a job and is read closely by future employers. A school certificate is „ein Schulzeugnis“ or „ein Abschlusszeugnis“, which shares the word „Zeugnis“ but not the purpose.

questions.stem: What does „die Gleitzeit“ mean in the world of work?
options: Flexitime
Part-time work
Parental leave
Overtime
questions.explanation: „Gleitzeit“ lets employees choose their start and finish times around fixed core hours. Part-time work is „die Teilzeit“, parental leave is „die Elternzeit“ and overtime is „die Überstunden“.

questions.stem: „Ich hatte mich bei einer Bank beworben, aber leider hat man mir eine Absage erteilt.“ What happened?
options: The bank offered the speaker a position
The bank invited the speaker to an interview
The bank asked the speaker to send a CV
The bank turned down the application
questions.explanation: „Eine Absage“ is a refusal, the opposite of „eine Zusage“ (an acceptance). „Leider“ signals the disappointing news before the noun confirms it.

questions.stem: What does „Nach dem Abitur lege ich ein Jahr Pause ein, bevor ich mich an der Uni einschreibe“ mean?
options: After the Abitur I am enrolling at university straight away for a year
After a year at university I am taking a break to sit the Abitur
After the Abitur I am taking a year to decide whether to leave school
After the Abitur I am taking a year off before enrolling at university
questions.explanation: „Eine Pause einlegen“ is to take a break, and „sich einschreiben“ is to enrol. „Bevor“ puts the break first and enrolment second, which is the order the distractors scramble.

questions.stem: What does „Er hat das Gymnasium abgebrochen“ mean?
options: He was suspended from the academic secondary school
He dropped out of the academic secondary school
He graduated from the academic secondary school
He transferred to the academic secondary school
questions.explanation: „Abbrechen“ is to break off, so „die Schule abbrechen“ is to leave without finishing. Graduating would be „das Abitur machen“ or „die Schule abschließen“; „das Gymnasium“ is a school, not a gym.

questions.stem: What does „Viele wünschen sich eine bessere Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf“ mean?
options: Many people want work and family life to be easier to combine
Many people want their families to support their careers more
Many people want better agreements between unions and employers
Many people want their children to choose better careers
questions.explanation: „Vereinbar“ means compatible, so „die Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf“ is how well the two fit together. It is a key term in the work-life balance debate, not a reference to formal agreements.

questions.stem: „Lebenslanges Lernen ist keine Option mehr, sondern eine Notwendigkeit. Wer sich nicht weiterbildet, bleibt auf der Strecke.“ What does the writer claim?
options: People who do not keep training will be left behind
Lifelong learning is a choice that only some workers need
Further training has become unnecessary in most careers
People who train too much lose sight of their own goals
questions.explanation: „Auf der Strecke bleiben“ is an idiom for falling by the wayside, so those who do not undertake further training get left behind. The „keine Option, sondern eine Notwendigkeit“ frame rules out the reading that it is optional.

questions.stem: „Viele Jugendliche wählen eine Ausbildung, weil sie sofort Geld verdienen wollen. Ein Studium dauert länger, öffnet aber andere Türen.“ What contrast is drawn?
options: Training takes longer than a university course but usually leads to better-paid work
University students earn money sooner than trainees usually do
University closes doors that a vocational training course would open
Training brings an income sooner; university takes longer but offers other options
questions.explanation: The first sentence links the Ausbildung to earning straight away, and „dauert länger, öffnet aber andere Türen“ concedes the cost of a Studium before naming its benefit. Reading „andere Türen“ as closed doors reverses the writer's point.

questions.stem: What does „Mir fällt es schwer, Schule, Nebenjob und Sport unter einen Hut zu bringen“ mean?
options: I have found school much harder since I started my part-time job
I would rather give up sport than my part-time job
I find school, work and sport all equally difficult
I find it hard to juggle school, a part-time job and sport
questions.explanation: „Unter einen Hut bringen“ (to bring under one hat) means to fit several demands together. „Es fällt mir schwer“ is 'I find it hard', and the idiom names the three things being balanced rather than comparing them.

questions.stem: What does „der Leistungsdruck“ mean?
options: A reward for strong results
A limit on the hours of study
Pressure to perform and achieve
A sudden drop in results
questions.explanation: „Die Leistung“ is performance or achievement and „der Druck“ is pressure. It is a common term in discussions of school stress and the Abitur.

questions.stem: What does „der Gruppenzwang“ mean?
options: Peer pressure
A compulsory group project
Team spirit
A club's membership rules
questions.explanation: „Der Zwang“ is compulsion, so „der Gruppenzwang“ is the pressure a group puts on a member to conform. Team spirit is „der Teamgeist“ or „der Zusammenhalt“.

questions.stem: What does „das Selbstwertgefühl“ mean?
options: Self-esteem
Selfishness
Self-discipline
Self-employment
questions.explanation: „Das Selbstwertgefühl“ is the feeling of one's own worth. Selfishness is „der Egoismus“ and self-employment is „die Selbstständigkeit“, which shares the „Selbst-“ prefix but nothing else.

questions.stem: What does „die Zukunftsangst“ mean?
options: Anxiety about the future
Excitement about the future
A plan for the future
A vision of the future
questions.explanation: „Die Zukunft“ is the future and „die Angst“ fear, so the compound names worry about what lies ahead, often in discussions of young people, jobs and the climate.

questions.stem: Which description best captures „die Geborgenheit“?
options: A cosy, sociable atmosphere among friends in a busy inn
A quiet pleasure at another person's bad luck
A feeling of being safe, sheltered and cared for
A feeling of longing for distant places
questions.explanation: „Geborgenheit“ is the security of being protected, often within a family. A cosy atmosphere is „Gemütlichkeit“ and pleasure at another's misfortune is „Schadenfreude“, two other terms without a direct English equivalent.

questions.stem: „Als Kind von Einwanderern sitze ich manchmal zwischen zwei Stühlen.“ What does the speaker mean?
options: She sometimes forgets which language she is speaking
She sometimes feels torn between two cultures
She sometimes feels unwelcome at both of her schools
She sometimes struggles to choose between two careers
questions.explanation: „Zwischen zwei Stühlen sitzen“ is to be caught between two sides. Coming straight after „Kind von Einwanderern“, the two sides are the culture of her parents and the culture she has grown up in.

questions.stem: What does „Die Pubertät ist eine Zeit, in der man sich von den Eltern abgrenzt“ say?
options: Adolescence is when parents set stricter limits on what their teenagers do
Adolescence is when young people grow closer to their parents
Adolescence is when teenagers start to resemble their parents
Adolescence is when young people set themselves apart from their parents
questions.explanation: „Sich abgrenzen“ is to distance or distinguish oneself. The reflexive „sich“ shows the young person is doing it; parents setting limits would be „Grenzen setzen“, which shares the root but not the meaning.

questions.stem: What does „Ich achte darauf, genug zu schlafen, aber vor Prüfungen gelingt mir das kaum“ mean?
options: I always sleep far too much in the weeks leading up to my exams
I never pay attention to how much sleep I get
I find exams easier once I have had enough sleep
I try to get enough sleep, but before exams I hardly manage it
questions.explanation: „Auf etwas achten“ is to make a point of something, and „es gelingt mir kaum“ means I hardly succeed. „Kaum“ is a near-negative, so the sentence describes failing to sleep enough, not sleeping too much.

questions.stem: What does „Meine Tante ist mein Vorbild, weil sie sich nie unterkriegen lässt“ mean?
options: My aunt is my role model because she never takes a day off work
My aunt is my role model because she never loses her temper
My aunt is my role model because she never lets things get her down
My aunt is my role model because she never lets other people speak first
questions.explanation: „Das Vorbild“ is a role model, and „sich nicht unterkriegen lassen“ is to refuse to be beaten down by difficulty. „Lassen“ here means to allow, as in letting something happen to oneself.

questions.stem: „Meine Oma sagt immer, früher sei alles besser gewesen. Dabei hatte sie als Kind weder Heizung noch fließendes Wasser.“ What does the writer imply?
options: That his grandmother's view of the past is not entirely realistic
That his grandmother would honestly prefer to live without heating today
That his own childhood was harder than his grandmother's
That his grandmother never likes talking about her childhood
questions.explanation: „Dabei“ here means 'and yet', setting a hard fact against her claim, so the writer quietly questions it. „Sei … gewesen“ reports her words in the subjunctive, which keeps them at a distance from the writer's own view.

questions.stem: What does „die Chancengleichheit“ mean?
options: Equal opportunity
A lucky coincidence
An equal share of the work
A tied result
questions.explanation: „Die Chance“ is an opportunity and „die Gleichheit“ is equality. It is a key term in discussions of education and rights; a lucky coincidence is „ein glücklicher Zufall“.

questions.stem: „Mit meinem Stiefvater bin ich anfangs nicht warm geworden, inzwischen kommen wir aber gut miteinander aus.“ What does the speaker say?
options: She got on well with her stepfather until they recently fell out
She did not warm to her stepfather at first, but they now get on well
Her stepfather was cold towards her at first and still is today
She and her stepfather have never really got on with each other
questions.explanation: „Mit jemandem warm werden“ is to warm to someone, and „gut miteinander auskommen“ is to get on well. „Anfangs … inzwischen“ (at first … by now) marks the change over time.

questions.stem: Which verb completes „Ich kann mich immer auf meine beste Freundin ___“ ('I can always rely on my best friend')?
options: verstehen
verlieben
verlassen
vertragen
questions.explanation: „Sich auf jemanden verlassen“ is to rely on someone; the preposition „auf“ is part of the verb's pattern. „Sich vertragen“ and „sich verstehen“ both take „mit“, and „sich verlieben“ takes „in“.

questions.stem: What does „Wir haben uns gestritten, uns aber schnell wieder vertragen“ mean?
options: We argued, but we soon made up again
We argued and have not spoken since
We agreed quickly, so we did not argue
We argued because we cannot stand each other
questions.explanation: „Sich streiten“ is to argue and „sich wieder vertragen“ is to make up. „Aber“ marks the contrast, so the friendship survived the argument.

questions.stem: What does „Freundschaften pflegen“ mean?
options: To keep friendships going
To care for friends who are ill
To make new friends quickly
To end a friendship politely
questions.explanation: „Pflegen“ is to look after or maintain, and with „Freundschaften“ it means keeping in touch and investing in friends. Nursing someone who is ill also uses „pflegen“, but takes a person as its object, not a friendship.

questions.stem: What does „Seit meine Eltern sich getrennt haben, wohne ich abwechselnd bei beiden“ mean?
options: Since my parents argued, I have wanted to move out of home
Since my parents moved away, I have visited them only in the school holidays
Since my parents separated, I have lived with each of them in turn
Since my parents separated, I have lived only with my mother
questions.explanation: „Sich trennen“ is to separate and „abwechselnd“ means alternately. „Seit“ with the present „wohne“ shows the arrangement is still going on, so English needs 'have lived'.

questions.stem: What is „eine Wohngemeinschaft (WG)“?
options: A public housing estate run by the local council
A family's holiday house in the country
A shared flat or house rented by several people
A retirement home for older people
questions.explanation: A WG is common among students and apprentices, who share a flat and its costs. A retirement home is „ein Altersheim“ or „Seniorenheim“, which shares the idea of living together but not the meaning.

questions.stem: What does „jemandem das Du anbieten“ mean?
options: To ask someone politely to stop calling you by your first name
To introduce yourself to someone formally
To invite someone to use the informal form of address
To speak to someone as if they were a child
questions.explanation: Moving from „Sie“ to „du“ is a step that one person, usually the older or more senior, offers. Until it is offered, „Sie“ remains the polite default between adults.

questions.stem: Which statement fits typical usage of „Sie“ and „du“ in Germany?
options: Teenagers address each other with „Sie“ until they become friends
Secondary students usually switch to „du“ with their teachers at sixteen
„Sie“ is reserved for speaking to people over about sixty
Adults meeting at work usually begin with „Sie“ until one offers „du“
questions.explanation: „Sie“ marks distance and respect between adults who are not close, so it is the default with colleagues, officials and teachers. Young people use „du“ with each other from the start, and age alone does not decide the choice.

questions.stem: In a role-play you meet your new manager, Frau Weber. Which question is appropriate?
options: „Guten Tag, Frau Weber. Könnten Sie mir sagen, wann ich anfangen soll?“
„Hallo Frau Weber. Kannst du mir sagen, wann ich anfangen soll?“
„Guten Tag, Frau Weber. Könntest du mir bitte sagen, wann ich anfangen soll?“
„Hi Frau Weber! Sag mal, wann soll ich denn anfangen?“
questions.explanation: A first meeting with a manager needs „Sie“ throughout, and „könnten Sie“ is the polite Konjunktiv II request. Pairing „Frau Weber“ with „du“ or „könntest du“ mixes formal and informal registers.

questions.stem: In a role-play, which phrase offers a compromise?
options: „Darf ich mich kurz vorstellen?“
„Wie wäre es, wenn wir uns die Kosten teilen?“
„Nein, das kommt für mich überhaupt nicht in Frage.“
„Da haben Sie völlig recht.“
questions.explanation: „Wie wäre es, wenn …?“ (How would it be if …?) puts forward a middle way, here sharing the cost. „Da haben Sie völlig recht“ simply agrees, which closes the discussion rather than negotiating it.

questions.stem: In a role-play, what is „Da muss ich Ihnen recht geben, allerdings …“ used for?
options: Conceding a point while keeping one's own position
Agreeing completely and ending the discussion
Asking the other speaker to explain their view
Rejecting the other speaker's point outright
questions.explanation: „Jemandem recht geben“ is to concede that someone is right, and „allerdings“ (however) signals that a reservation follows. Conceding before qualifying keeps a negotiation cooperative.

questions.stem: In a negotiation, what is „Lass uns noch einmal auf das Taschengeld zurückkommen“ used for?
options: To refuse to discuss pocket money any further
To revisit an issue that has not yet been resolved
To close the conversation in a friendly way
To confirm an outcome both speakers have accepted
questions.explanation: „Auf etwas zurückkommen“ is to come back to a point. The study design names revisiting unresolved issues as a strategy, and this phrase does it without sounding confrontational.

questions.stem: Which sentence confirms an agreed outcome at the end of a negotiation?
options: „Also abgemacht: Ich darf bis elf bleiben, wenn ich dich anrufe.“
„Darüber müssen wir aber unbedingt bald noch einmal genauer reden.“
„Was hältst du eigentlich von meinem Vorschlag?“
„Ich sehe das leider immer noch ganz anders.“
questions.explanation: „Abgemacht“ (agreed, it's a deal) followed by the terms sums up the result for both speakers. Asking „Was hältst du von meinem Vorschlag?“ invites a response, so the negotiation is still open.

questions.stem: Your partner says „Am Samstag kann ich dir das Auto nicht leihen.“ Which reply negotiates instead of simply repeating your request?
options: „Dann frage ich eben jemand anderen danach.“
„Und wenn ich es nur am Abend nehme und vollgetankt zurückbringe?“
„Aber ich brauche das Auto am Samstag unbedingt!“
„Warum bist du eigentlich immer so streng mit mir und meinen Plänen?“
questions.explanation: „Und wenn …?“ proposes a condition that gives the other person something in return, which is a compromise. Insisting with „unbedingt“ only restates the demand and gives the partner no reason to change their mind.

questions.stem: Which phrase best links your next point to what the other speaker has just said?
options: „Übrigens wollte ich etwas ganz anderes sagen: …“
„Zum Schluss möchte ich mich herzlich bedanken: …“
„Zuerst möchte ich mich kurz vorstellen: …“
„Um auf Ihren Punkt mit den Kosten einzugehen: …“
questions.explanation: „Auf etwas eingehen“ is to respond to a point, so this phrase builds on the other speaker's words. „Übrigens“ (by the way) changes the subject, which is the opposite of linking.

questions.stem: In a discussion, what is „Habe ich Sie richtig verstanden, dass …?“ used for?
options: Asking the other speaker to speak more slowly and clearly
Changing the subject of the discussion to a new point
Checking that you have understood the other speaker correctly
Telling the other speaker politely that they are mistaken
questions.explanation: The question restates what you think the other person meant so they can confirm or correct it. Clarifying before responding is one of the strategies for keeping an exchange on track.

questions.stem: „Ich finde, du übertreibst ein bisschen. Natürlich will ich lernen, aber ein Abend pro Woche mit Freunden muss doch drin sein.“ What is the speaker doing?
options: Asking to give up study to see friends more often
Apologising for spending too many evenings out
Pushing back while asking for one free evening a week
Agreeing to study every evening of the week
questions.explanation: „Du übertreibst“ (you are exaggerating) challenges the other view, and „muss doch drin sein“ is a colloquial way of saying something should be possible. „Natürlich will ich lernen“ concedes a point first, a typical negotiation move.
